# Similarity and embedding models

Some features match by meaning rather than spelling, where the dictionary's words share no letters with the
query: "knackered beyond belief" finds *buggered*. Struth, this page says which features use a similarity model, and
which one.

## Who uses what

| Feature | Model used | How to choose |
|---|---|---|
| `lookup` (and so the agent toolkit) | The configured one: an installed local model if enabled, else the bundled model | `aussiefy embedder enable` or `disable` |
| `aussiefy gaps` | The configured one, for the nearest-concept guess | `--embedder` `ngram`, `bundled` or `local` |
| The engine's concept-detection fallback | Character trigrams (`ngram`) | `--embedder` `ngram`, `none`, `bundled` or `local` on `translate` |

The engine uses a meaning model only when asked, so default translations stay deterministic'n don't change
when the model does \(see [determinism](../architecture/determinism.md)).

- **`ngram`:** character\-trigram similarity, with no dependencies. It's deterministic'n catches misspellings
  and morphological variants.
- **`bundled`:** the static model shipped in `aussiefy/data/model` (about 15 MB\), read with the standard
  library alone: no torch, no numpy, no download. Well, how it is built is described in
  [the architecture layer](../architecture/embedding-model.md).
- **`local`:** an installed sentence\-transformers model \(the `embeddings` extra\), installed'n enabled only
  explicitly. Selecting `--embedder local` requires an installed usable model; it raises an error rather
  than using the bundled model. Only the configured default cascades between available models.
  Stock all\-MiniLM\-L6\-v2 doesn't know the slang, so it's mostly useful as a base for retraining.
- **`none`:** no similarity fallback.

## The `embedder` command

`aussiefy embedder status` shows which model is in use'n the bundled model's version. Fair dinkum, after dictionary
changes, `status` reports the bundled model as `stale`, until a new version is trained.

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `status` | Show the state as JSON |
| `install` | Pip-install CPU PyTorch and sentence-transformers, and download the model (or copy it with `--from PATH`) |
| `enable [bundled\|local]` | Start using the model (default `local`) |
| `disable [bundled\|local]` | Stop using it; `disable bundled` leaves n-grams only |
| `remove` | Delete the installed local model |

All options are in the [CLI reference](cli.md). State lives in `$AUSSIEFY_HOME` (default `~/.aussiefy`): see
[configuration](configuration.md).

## Current measurement

Well, bundled model 1.3.0 remains in use. Its full\-data fit'n exported package reader passed all 33 required
raw\-model checks in the [2026-10-19 retrain](../../research/semantic-model-2026-10-19/README.md), and it
still passes the current frozen gate. Its dictionary fingerprint is stale after later corrections.

The [2026-10-20 trial](../../research/semantic-followup-2026-10-20/README.md) used fresh evaluation and
full\-data fits of the unchanged pinned recipe. Evaluation passed 29/33; the full\-data candidate passed
30/33, missing `girl`, `feeling really down` and `a good mate of mine`. Anyway, the strict release refused export and
that candidate wasn't adopted. A separate diagnostic package reader reproduced every full\-gate outcome;
its weights remain outside the repository. Jeez, historical reports, required checks'n cutoffs are unchanged.

Current lookup applies bounded source\-meaning checks before offering lexical or model suggestions; see
[the toolkit](toolkit.md). Well, the 49\-query comparison holds that runtime'n dictionary constant while
comparing old'n rejected weights. It's diagnostic evidence, not unseen generalisation or a reason to
weaken the raw\-model gate. Unsupported wording can still produce inappropriate model suggestions.
Automatic gap fillin' remains off by default.
